clue.text: Undisputed big guns? Not after this story!

definitions.text: Undisputed big guns? Not after this story!

parts.words: Undisputed big guns? Not after this story!
parts.note: the novel's title, read cryptically, says the greats (the big guns) were, past tense: once you have read the story, they are big guns no longer

explanation.walkthrough: Read the title as THE GREAT GAT'S BY: the great gat (gun) is by, meaning past or gone. So the undisputed big guns are a thing of the past once the story is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitzgerald's Jazz Age novel is the story in question, and its title doubles as a remark about big guns being bygone.

clue.text: Reason why some dilettante got ripped?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wondering why an amateur dabbler has suddenly bulked up at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-indulgent venture undertaken for vanity is a motive: the question mark hints that pride may explain the dabbler's new muscles.

clue.text: When using Dictaphone, put up level

indicators.note: a Dictaphone records speech, so the words are spoken rather than written, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: to put up is to raise

explanation.surface: An office worker dictating an instruction to put something up level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'level' looks like an adjective meaning flat, but it is the verb meaning demolish.
explanation.definitionFit: To level a building is to flatten it to the ground, which is the sense of demolishing completely.

clue.text: What's needed to screw tout le monde in French scheme

parts.note: French for everybody, which is all in English
the French word for in is en
a key is an explanatory scheme or diagram, as on a map

explanation.surface: Seems to ask what everyone in a French plan needs to tighten screws.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase must be translated into English, while 'in French' gives the French word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: This hexagonal L-shaped tool is used to turn socket-head screws, so it is what is needed to tighten them.

clue.text: Turn up with medal-winner from south Belvedere

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a zag is a sharp turn, as in zigzag

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means reading upwards

parts.note: an OBE is an honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, whose holder receives a medal

explanation.surface: Someone turning up at a stately home with an honours recipient.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are turned in this down clue: ZAG becomes GAZ and OBE becomes EBO.
explanation.definitionFit: A belvedere is a summerhouse or turret built to command a view, and this garden pavilion is the same kind of structure.

clue.text: Loathe debt, so ordered set menu

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A diner who hates owing money and so chooses the cheap fixed-price option.
explanation.definitionFit: In a restaurant this French phrase names a fixed-price meal of several courses, a set menu.

clue.text: Flatter schoolboy winning pound

indicators.note: the schoolboy wins, so takes in, the pound

parts.note: Billy Bunter is the greedy fat schoolboy of Frank Richards' Greyfriars stories
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Sucking up to a schoolboy who has just won some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like the verb to praise insincerely, but it is the comparative of an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A less sharp edge or a duller blade is flatter, and a more plain-spoken remark is likewise flatter in the sense of more direct.

clue.text: Charm rogue taken in by a supporter twice

indicators.note: the rogue is held between the two pairs of letters
twice says the a-plus-supporter pair is written a second time

parts.note: a stays as written and a bra is a supporting garment, so the pair gives a then bra
the same a and bra (a supporting garment) written again, as twice demands
a cad is a rogue or bounder

explanation.surface: A charming rogue is duped by someone who backs him twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a magic incantation, a spell or charm uttered by conjurors.

clue.text: For common Latin name, try Naked Azalea (found in New Zealand)

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: the stripped shrub sits inside the abbreviation
naked means stripped of its outer layer, so the first and last letters go

explanation.surface: Reads like botanical advice on finding the scientific name for a bare shrub growing in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin name' suggests a botanical label, but it means a surname from Latin America.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the most widespread Hispanic surnames, so a very common Latin American family name.

clue.text: Description of book written by rock band

indicators.note: the book's letter is placed by, beside, the band's name

parts.note: Blur is a 1990s English Britpop band

explanation.surface: A description of a book written by members of a rock group.
explanation.walkthrough: The blurb describes a book, so 'of book' can also be read as part of the definition, with book doing double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The short promotional summary printed on a book jacket is a description of its contents.

clue.text: Half-blown fuse to ruin basket in living room

indicators.note: only the first half of the word survives, the rest blown away

parts.note: to coalesce is to fuse or merge
to scuttle is to ruin, as with plans or a ship

explanation.surface: An electrical fuse partly blown threatens to wreck something in the lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: Only COAL, the first half of COALESCE, is used.
explanation.definitionFit: This fireside container holds fuel by the hearth, a kind of bucket or basket kept in a sitting room.

clue.text: British heading off on hols

indicators.note: the first letter is removed

parts.note: hols, short for holidays, can be tours

explanation.surface: British holidaymakers setting off on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: To a British speaker, things British belong to us, the possessive pronoun covering our own nation.

clue.text: According to court, missing hip muscle caused back cracking

parts.note: in means fashionable or hip
an ab is an abdominal muscle
sent can mean caused to become, as in sent him mad

indicators.note: the excellent label is written backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or cracking, written AI

explanation.surface: Medical complaint: a hip muscle injury made someone's back crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hip' looks anatomical but means trendy; 'cracking' means excellent, as A1.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin legal phrase describes proceedings held while the defendant is absent, so missing as courts put it.

clue.text: 20's ruler getting loads of grief about Queen?

parts.note: big suggests large in amount, loads of

indicators.note: the trouble goes round the royal letter

parts.note: bother is grief or trouble
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A ruler having lots of trouble over a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is DYSTOPIA; the answer is the leader of Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's all-seeing figurehead rules Oceania, the archetypal nightmare society that 20 across names.

clue.text: Spoiled, with diameter awry?

indicators.note: the letters are knocked out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A wheel or plate ruined because its diameter is off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoiled by having a diameter out of true would be uneven, one side heavier or higher than the other.

clue.text: Assistant chasing knighted thespian guide…

indicators.note: the assistant comes after the actor

parts.note: Sir Antony Sher was a knighted Shakespearean actor
a PA is a personal assistant

explanation.surface: A helper following a famous knighted actor around.
explanation.definitionFit: These Himalayan mountain people are famous as porters and escorts for climbers on Everest, hence a guide.

clue.text: Man told Asian with foot stuck above head where stretchers are?

indicators.note: told means spoken aloud, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: Jim is a man's name

indicators.note: in this down clue the last letter, the foot, moves to the top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man instructing an Asian contortionist to put a foot above his head.
explanation.walkthrough: ASIAN with its last letter moved to the front gives NASIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretchers here are people doing stretches, and gym halls are where they exercise; the question mark flags the pun on stretchers.

clue.text: …and what he does close to apoplectic members

indicators.note: the end letter of the word

parts.note: its last letter is C
limbs are members of the body

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: the guide's activity is near to enraging his limbs.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 16 across: 'he' is the Sherpa guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sherpa's work is ascending mountains, so ascending is what he does.

clue.text: Plunge one metre into river, not touching bottom

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the metre goes inside the river
in a down clue the bottom is the last letter, which is left off

parts.note: the Mersey is a river in north-west England flowing past Liverpool

explanation.surface: A wader stepping a metre into a river and finding no footing.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge something into liquid is to submerge or dip it completely.

clue.text: Nightmare as State knocked back help outside year block

indicators.note: the reversed help goes round the other letters
the word for help is turned backwards

parts.note: aid is help
to stop is to block

explanation.surface: A state that refused aid and blocked a year's progress becomes a nightmare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns the word for help round, and 'outside' wraps that reversal round the year and the block.
explanation.definitionFit: An imagined society of oppression and misery is the opposite of utopia, a nightmarish nation.

clue.text: Prefect joins Head of School for PE activity

indicators.note: the two pieces are put together

parts.note: Pontius Pilate was the Roman prefect of Judaea

indicators.note: the head of something is its top or front, so only the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: its first letter is S

explanation.surface: A school prefect teams up with the head teacher for a gym lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prefect' suggests a senior pupil, but it is the Roman governor's title.
explanation.definitionFit: This body-conditioning exercise system is a form of physical exercise, the sort of thing done in physical education.

clue.text: Wise words from this student embarking on ordinary career

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

indicators.note: the student gets on board, going inside

parts.note: to career is to race
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Sage advice for a student starting out on an ordinary career.
explanation.definitionFit: At Delphi the priestess or shrine delivered prophecies, so wise pronouncements came from this source.

clue.text: Instrument from arrangement of baritone music? Not so

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged
the following word's letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion
sic is Latin for thus or so

explanation.surface: Asks whether a baritone's arrangement counts as music, then says it doesn't.
explanation.walkthrough: MUSIC without SIC leaves MU, and BARITONE plus MU are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This jingling hand drum is a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Defect reported in nutty ingredient

indicators.note: reported means said aloud, a sound-alike in a non-rhotic accent

parts.note: a flaw is a defect

explanation.surface: A fault reported in a nut-based food product.
explanation.definitionFit: This layer of yeast on maturing sherry gives fino and amontillado their nutty tang, an ingredient of the flavour.

clue.text: Drop by grave … RIP

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a droplet of weeping shed at a graveside
second meaning: rip as a verb, to rend

explanation.walkthrough: RIP looks like the gravestone abbreviation, but it is the verb rip.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a teardrop shed in grief and, said differently, a verb meaning to rip apart.

clue.text: Fly beyond large tree

indicators.note: the cunning word comes after

parts.note: fly means knowing or cunning, as does arch

explanation.surface: An insect flying past a big tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like the insect or the verb, but it is the adjective meaning sly.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciduous conifer with needles that drop in winter.

clue.text: Class defends sticky tape

indicators.note: the class surrounds and protects the other word

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary social class
set means congealed or firm, as sticky jam sets

explanation.surface: A class at school sticks up for using adhesive tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticky tape' seems a single phrase, but sticky is wordplay and tape the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An audio cassette holds magnetic recording tape, so the word is used for the tape itself.

clue.text: Did he solo My Sweet Lord or share playing with e.g. Ringo?

definitions.text: Did he solo My Sweet Lord

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with, rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether the singer of a hit performed it alone or split it with his bandmate.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Beatles guitarist released My Sweet Lord as his first solo single in 1970.
